summary: BI-9252B9EA, D2 of EP-862820FD. Migration 20260828210000_add_employment_jurisdiction_to_work_location adds WorkLocation.jurisdictionSlug: which employment jurisdiction governs work done at a location. No column anywhere on the worker path said which employment rules apply, so the co-employment control (BI-B506AD2E) had nothing to look a rule up by. This is a property of a PLACE, not of a person: it says where the organisation has put a role, and it is set by an operator configuring their own locations. It becomes an input to a determination ABOUT a worker, which is why it is declared here rather than treated as ordinary configuration, but it collects nothing new about any data subject and it is not derived from any worker's address, residence or personal record. The column is a String on the same closed PROFESSION_JURISDICTIONS vocabulary that Organization.employsIn and RegulatoryAutonomyPolicy.jurisdiction already carry, so the resolved value is accepted directly as the policy key with no translation layer between them. The migration backfills nothing: every existing row stays NULL and surfaces as named operator work, because inferring a jurisdiction from an address or timezone - or defaulting to 'global', which is a real member of the vocabulary and would return the permissive floor from a policy lookup - writes a confidently wrong legal answer into the database.

fields.name: jurisdictionSlug
fields.reason: An attribute of an organisational location, not of a data subject. It records which employment jurisdiction governs work done at that place - the same organisational scope Organization.employsIn already declares at the company level, narrowed to one site. It is not derived from any worker's home address, residence or personal record, and no worker's personal data is read to populate it. WorkLocation is classified public and this field does not change that: a location's country is not confidential and appears on job postings.
fields.provenance: Set by an operator when they configure a work location. Never inferred: not from the location's Address, not from its timezone, not from the organisation's first employsIn entry. The migration writes no value at all - every existing row is left NULL and reads as the typed unresolved reason 'location-without-jurisdiction'.
